shortDescription: Strings feel excessively high off the fretboard, requiring painful finger pressure to fret chords.

q_action_location.title: Where Action Feels Hardest
q_action_location.question: Where on the neck does fretting feel the most uncomfortably high and stiff?
q_action_location.measurementGuide: Try an open F major barre chord at fret 1, then play chords at fret 12.

options.label: At the 1st fret (Open F barre chord hurts hand)
options.description: Fretting near the nut takes excessive force; notes go sharp when pressed.

options.label: In the middle of the neck (Frets 5 to 9)
options.description: Strings bow dramatically away from the fretboard like an archery bow.

options.label: High up the neck (Frets 12 and above)
options.description: Action gets progressively higher toward the body and bridge.

nut_slots_too_high.title: Nut Slots Cut Too Shallow
rankedCauses: Factory nut left intentionally tall for safe transport
Replacement nut installed without final slot depth dressing
fixOrder: Fret the 3rd fret and observe clearance between string bottom and 1st fret wire.
Clearance should be almost touching (approx 0.15mm, thickness of paper).
Carefully deepen slots with appropriate gauge nut files angled slightly back toward tuners.
nut_slots_too_high.whenToConsultLuthier: Filing nut slots too deep causes open string buzz and requires replacing the nut.

excessive_neck_relief.title: Excessive Neck Relief (Forward Bow)
rankedCauses: Truss rod too loose against string tension
High humidity causing neck wood to swell into forward bow
fixOrder: Tighten truss rod clockwise (righty-tighty) by 1/4 turn.
Allow neck 15 minutes to adjust, retune to pitch, and recheck action.
measurementsRequired: Capo fret 1, hold fret 17, check gap at fret 7 (target 0.25mm - 0.35mm).
excessive_neck_relief.whenToConsultLuthier: If truss rod cannot turn or feels stripped.

bridge_saddles_too_high.title: Bridge Saddles / Acoustic Saddle Set Too High
rankedCauses: Bridge height thumbscrews or saddle screws set too high
Acoustic saddle bone blank not sanded down to correct height
fixOrder: For electrics: lower saddle screws or bridge posts by 1/2 turn counter-clockwise.
For acoustics: mark bottom of bone saddle, sand bottom evenly on flat sandpaper surface (sanding 1mm off saddle lowers 12th fret action by 0.5mm).
bridge_saddles_too_high.whenToConsultLuthier: If bridge saddles are bottomed out and neck angle requires a neck reset or pocket shim.
